Title: Verify that OTP generation for worker activation is rejected if the requesting user has no pending shop change request
Section: Worker Management - OTP Generation and Verification
Preconditions: User is authenticated as a shop owner with no pending shop change request for the target shop
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers/send-otp with the payload in testData, replacing {shopId} with a valid shop ID owned by the user.

Test Data: {
  "name": "Test Worker",
  "email": "testworker@example.com",
  "phoneNumber": "+8801700000000",
  "role": "TAILOR"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: You don't have any pending add/change worker request'. No OTP is sent to the worker's email or phone.

Preconditions: User is authenticated as a shop owner with no pending shop change request for the target shop. A worker exists with a valid OTP.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers/set-pin with the payload in testData, replacing {shopId} with a valid shop ID not associated with the user's pending request.

Test Data: {
  "phoneNumber": "+8801700000000",
  "otp": "123456",
  "pin": "1234",
  "confirmPin": "1234"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: You don't have permission to modify this shop'. The worker's PIN is not set.

Title: Verify that adding a worker with malicious input (e.g., SQL injection, script tags) in name or address is rejected or sanitized
Preconditions: User is authenticated as a shop owner with a pending shop change request for the target shop.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the payload in testData, replacing {shopId} with a valid shop ID owned by the user.

Test Data: {
  "name": "Test Worker<script>alert('xss')</script>",
  "email": "testworker@example.com",
  "phoneNumber": "+8801700000000",
  "role": "TAILOR",
  "address": "123 Main St; DROP TABLE workers;--"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Invalid input'. The worker is not created, or the malicious input is stored as plain text (not executed).

Title: Verify that retrieving workers by shop ID enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference) - unauthorized user cannot access another shop's worker list
Preconditions: User is authenticated as a shop owner or worker. Shop A and Shop B exist, and the user is associated with Shop A only.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers?page=0&limit=10, replacing {shopId} with the ID of Shop B.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found), and the response body contains a generic error message (e.g., 'Access denied' or 'Shop not found'). No worker data for Shop B is returned.

Title: Verify that adding a worker with an existing email from the same shop returns an error and does not proceed
Preconditions: User is authenticated as a shop owner with a pending shop change request for the target shop. A worker with the same email already exists in the shop.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the payload in testData, replacing {shopId} with a valid shop ID owned by the user.

Test Data: {
  "name": "Test Worker",
  "email": "existingworker@example.com",
  "phoneNumber": "+8801700000001",
  "role": "TAILOR"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Worker Already assigned to this shop'. No OTP is sent, and no new worker record is created.
